source: Lets start with a simple baseplate where the player is a physics based vehicle, for now no model but I want to have the player to be spawned into a floating part resembling the sizes of a scooter

answers.ask: How large should the baseplate be - the Studio default, or something bigger to drive around on?
answers.answer: Use the Studio default baseplate size for now; this is just a simple physics vehicle test area.

answers.ask: No theme was stated, and you asked for no model yet - should the baseplate stay untextured grey placeholder?
answers.answer: Yes, keep the baseplate as an untextured grey placeholder for now, with no vehicle model beyond the floating scooter-sized part.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: How large should the baseplate be - the Studio default, or something bigger to drive around on? A: Use the Studio default baseplate size for now; this is just a simple physics vehicle test area.
- [author] theme — Q: No theme was stated, and you asked for no model yet - should the baseplate stay untextured grey placeholder? A: Yes, keep the baseplate as an untextured grey placeholder for now, with no vehicle model beyond the floating scooter-sized part.

## Enriched image prompt
Build a minimal physics-vehicle test area consisting only of the Studio-default-sized baseplate as a flat, untextured grey surface. At the centre, leave clear spawn space for one simple floating primitive part approximately the footprint of a scooter, with no finished vehicle mesh or additional scenery. Keep the entire plate empty, level, unobstructed, and visually placeholder-like so movement and physics behaviour can be tested without other geometry.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Simulation because the requested activity is testing and operating a physics-based vehicle.

## Shape and preset
Use `space-bounded`, Zone (Bounded Play Space), taken from outside Simulation's usual shape set: the whole activity occurs on one finite flat baseplate. Preset is none because the minimal placeholder test does not request the contraptions, hazards, or circulation of the Physics Sim preset.

## Config requirements
No canonical image option applies. The Studio-default-sized grey baseplate and one scooter-sized floating primitive player part are the complete visible geometry; adding roads, ramps, props, structures, or thematic dressing would contradict the author.

## Layout requirements
Use a free-text SpawnZone placement at the centre of the baseplate, positioned to instantiate the scooter-sized floating player part slightly above the surface with clear space on every side. No other post-segmentation placement is required.

## Layout components
The build has one flat rectangular baseplate, an open unobstructed driving surface, a simple map edge, and one centred floating scooter-sized primitive. Compose the full plate in frame so its intentionally empty test-area character is unambiguous.

## Render order
Use `isometric`: the one-surface layout has no topology to validate, and the simple plate-plus-part composition is authoritative.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Use medium scale because the Studio default baseplate is the requested extent while the scooter-sized part must remain visible. The theme is neutral untextured grey prototyping geometry. Only `P0` is required: this is one flat bounded surface with no overhang, interior transition, or separate map.
